page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU and 4 GB of RAM. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The single physical core operates without hyperthreading, providing a dedicated thread with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance but limited multi-threaded capabilities due to the single-vCPU constraint. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average range, as do single-threaded gzip compression and text processing. However, multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, register in the bottom 10% of performance. Passmark CPU, memory, and database operations also rank in the lower percentiles. For lightweight machine learning, LLM inference with a small 135M model achieves an average text generation speed of 85.18 tokens per second, though prompt processing is weak at 179.0 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-1 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources. The primary tradeoff is the severe bottleneck on multi-threaded tasks and database operations, alongside the lack of local NVMe storage. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, simple text processing, or small-scale background utility tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or parallel processing.
